form.paragraph: This review integrates the state of the art across three axes of precision weeding—chemical, physical, and image-AI—through the lens of detection–actuation matching. We formalize this concept with a latency-budget model and analyze 132 studies to compare efficacy, cost, and environmental impact. We highlight the bottleneck of detection versus actuation and propose design archetypes based on herbicide selectivity, using garlic and onion as a case study to identify gaps in academic validation.
novelty: Integration of chemical, physical, and image-AI methods in precision weeding.
Introduction of a first-order latency-budget model for detection-actuation matching.
Identification of herbicide selectivity as a key determinant in system design.
Design guidelines tailored to specific crop conditions.
